List, Get and Set Controls

Source: R/accessors.R
controls.Rd

Reads and changes the settings an object of class objfn, parfn, prdfn or obsfn was built with. controls(x) lists the available controls; with name, the value of that control is returned or replaced. Elements of a list or data frame value can be changed with $ or [].

Usage

controls(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'objfn'
controls(x, name = NULL, condition = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fn'
controls(x, condition = NULL, name = NULL, ...)

controls(x, ...) <- value

# S3 method for class 'objfn'
controls(x, name, condition = NULL, ...) <- value

# S3 method for class 'fn'
controls(x, condition = NULL, name, ...) <- value

Arguments

x

object of class objfn or fn.

...

not used.

name

character, the name of the control. Default NULL lists the controls.

condition

character, the condition name. Default NULL, every condition.

value

the new value of the control.

Value

For an fn, controls(x) prints the available controls and returns them invisibly, a list with one entry per function; for an objfn, it returns their names. With name, the value of the control, or NULL if no function holds it. The setter returns x.

Details

A control belongs to the function built with it and is shared by every sum or composition that contains this function. Changing it on one of them changes it for all of them.

On an fn, the lookup covers the functions x is made of, e.g. the factors of g * x * p. condition restricts it to the functions defined for that condition; a function built without a condition counts for every condition. With condition = NULL, the getter returns the value of the first function that holds the control and the setter changes every function that holds it. On an objfn, including sums, scaled objectives and objectives composed with a parameter transformation, the lookup covers the objective terms and the functions they evaluate: the prediction and error model given to normL2() and the parameter transformation of an objfn * parfn. The solver tolerances of an objective can so be changed without the prediction function it was built from. A control of the objective term itself is found first. Setting a control that no function holds is an error, as is an unknown condition.

The second positional argument is name for an objfn and condition for an fn; name both arguments to avoid confusion.

See also

normL2(), P(), Y()

Examples

old <- options(dMod2.outdir = tempdir())

## parfn with condition
p <- P(eqnvec(x = "-a*x"), method = "implicit", condition = "C1")
controls(p)
#> C1:
#> [1] "keepRoot"    "controlsPTC"
controls(p, condition = "C1", name = "keepRoot")
#> [1] TRUE
controls(p, condition = "C1", name = "keepRoot") <- FALSE

## obsfn without condition
g <- Y(g = eqnvec(y = "s*x"), f = NULL, states = "x", parameters = "s")
controls(g)
#> :
#> [1] "attachInput"
controls(g, name = "attachInput")
#> [1] FALSE
controls(g, name = "attachInput") <- TRUE

options(old)
